import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Source file paths
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/test_1.csv"
    target_output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Columns expected in sources and target (all identical)
    columns = ['tripduration', 'starttime', 'stoptime', 'start station id', 'start station name',
               'start station latitude', 'start station longitude', 'end station id', 'end station name',
               'end station latitude', 'end station longitude', 'bikeid', 'usertype', 'birth year', 'gender']

    # Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
    df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
    df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

    # Confirm schemas are identical and columns match target schema
    # (Given by prompt, so no renaming needed)

    # Since both sources have exactly the same schema as the target,
    # we can simply concatenate (union) the two dataframes vertically.

    # Concatenate source dataframes
    df = pd.concat([df0, df1], ignore_index=True)

    # Ensure data types match target schema:
    # Target schema types:
    # 'tripduration': integer
    # 'starttime': string
    # 'stoptime': string
    # 'start station id': integer
    # 'start station name': string
    # 'start station latitude': float
    # 'start station longitude': float
    # 'end station id': integer
    # 'end station name': string
    # 'end station latitude': float
    # 'end station longitude': float
    # 'bikeid': integer
    # 'usertype': string
    # 'birth year': integer
    # 'gender': integer

    # Convert columns to appropriate types, handling missing or malformed data gracefully

    # Integer columns
    int_cols = ['tripduration', 'start station id', 'end station id', 'bikeid', 'birth year', 'gender']
    for col in int_cols:
        # Convert to numeric, coerce errors to NaN, then convert to Int64 (nullable integer dtype)
        df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

    # Float columns
    float_cols = ['start station latitude', 'start station longitude', 'end station latitude', 'end station longitude']
    for col in float_cols:
        df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)

    # String columns
    str_cols = ['starttime', 'stoptime', 'start station name', 'end station name', 'usertype']
    for col in str_cols:
        # Convert to string, fill NaN with empty string to avoid issues
        df[col] = df[col].astype(str).fillna('')

    # Optional: Strip whitespace from string columns to match target formatting
    for col in str_cols:
        df[col] = df[col].str.strip()

    # Save the combined dataframe to the target CSV path with header and no index
    df.to_csv(target_output_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
